Weather tracker: February temperature records broken in France and Spain
This article is more than 5 months old
Daniel Harris and Claire Jones
text:
The end of winter brought unseasonably high temperatures across much of Europe but particularly so in northern Spain and south-west France as numerous February temperatures records were broken.
Cities across Nouvelle-Aquitaine and the Basque Country, including Bordeaux, Bilbao and San Sebastián, matched or exceeded their long-term February records, with temperatures of 27.1C and 27.6C recorded in Bilbao and San Sebastián on Wednesday, more than 13C above average for the time of year.
The highest temperature of the spell was recorded on Tuesday in Saint Gladie at the foot of the Pyrenees mountains, where the mercury hit 29.6C, 16C above average and 2.6C above the previous highest February temperature at this station.
The warmth across western Europe was the result of a large area of high pressure developing across central Europe, which brought southerly winds across western Europe.
Temperatures across northern Spain and south-west France were then further enhanced by the Föhn effect, a meteorological phenomenon whereby air that is forced over a mountain range sinks downwards on the leeward side, becoming significantly warmer and drier as a result.
After a reduction in temperatures over the weekend, further unseasonable warm temperatures are expected this week across much of Europe as high pressure is expected to remain across the continent. This will bring temperatures widely into the teens and low 20s, often 5-10C above the average temperatures for early March.
Meanwhile, north China’s Hebei province put out a level 4 emergency response on Sunday in preparation for incoming heavy snowfall. Heavy snow was forecast for Sunday into Monday with blizzard conditions and up to 10-20cm of snow, which could disrupt transportation and urban service.
This heavy snowfall was then expected to move eastwards and affect much of South Korea on Monday. The heavy snow is due to the influence of a low-pressure system passing south of Jeju Island. Gangwon’s Yeongdong region is expected to see the heaviest snow as the winds are from the east. The snow could continue into Tuesday with up to 5cm an hour possible. Mountain areas in Gangwon could record 10-30cm of snow, with up to 40cm locally.
